# syncTopologyBar destroys toolbar-owned items, orphaning vdom stubs

## Context

@tobiu pulled `dev`, ran `build all`, opened `apps/workstation`, and hit three symptoms at once: grids intermittently empty, dock drag-zone styling absent, and repeated errors in the App Worker console — while CI was green. He asked whether it was caching.

It is not caching. `dev @ c74a53b6d0` (#18546, merged ~2h before this filing) leaves three destroyed components as live `{componentId}` placeholders in the topology toolbar's vdom. Every subsequent Workstation viewport vdom sync walks into one and throws, so updates stop landing.

Observed on the operator's own instance (Chrome, `localhost:8082`, 1675x1084) via Neural Link:

```
util.VDom.getVdom: Component not found for id: neo-component-35
  at VDom.getVdom (src/util/VDom.mjs:308)
  at VDom.syncVdomState (src/util/VDom.mjs:451)   <- Array.map over childNodes
  at VDom.syncVdomState (src/util/VDom.mjs:467)
  at Viewport.syncVdomState (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:893)
  at Viewport.syncVnodeTree (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:928)
  at Viewport.afterSetVnode (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:125)
  -> Viewport.executeVdomUpdate (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:378)
```

Independently reproduced on a second origin (`localhost:8080`, different browser engine, virgin IndexedDB, fresh SharedWorker), where it threw the same error at `initVnode` on `neo-component-34`. **Two origins, two browsers, empty vs. persisted storage, same defect** — this falsifies caching, stale SharedWorker, and stale persisted topology as causes. Live-open sweep: latest 20 open issues checked at 2026-09-09T17:18:40Z, no equivalent found.

## The Problem

Runtime state of the topology bar on the operator's instance:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `query_vdom({id: 'neo-toolbar-1'})` | `vdom.cn` = **5** children: `neo-button-33`, `neo-button-34`, `neo-component-35`, `neo-button-35`, `neo-button-36` |
| `find_instances({parentId: 'neo-toolbar-1'})` | **2** live instances — `neo-button-33` (Save workspace), `neo-button-34` (Close workspace) |
| `get_component_tree` | `neo-component-35` absent from the tree entirely |

Three of the five vdom children reference components that no longer exist. `VDom.getVdom` throws on the first one it maps.

The user-visible consequences are all downstream of that one throw: the viewport's vdom sync aborts, so class and style deltas never reach the DOM (no dock styling), projected content never lands (empty grids), and Undo/Redo are gone from the topology bar because they were destroyed outright.

**Why the observation is intermittent:** the throw happens on a viewport-level sync. Whether a given interaction is visibly broken depends on whether it needed a viewport-rooted update, which is why it reads as "sometimes".

## The Architectural Reality

The view declares two things on one config (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`, `createTopologyBar()`):

```javascript
{
    ntype  : 'toolbar',
    actions: [{action: 'undo', ...}, {action: 'redo', ...}],
    items  : [{ntype: 'button', handler: 'saveTopology',  text: 'Save workspace'},
              {ntype: 'button', handler: 'closeTopology', text: 'Close workspace'}],
    reference: 'topology-toolbar'
}
```

`toolbar.Base:201` merges `...me.createActionItemConfigs()` into `items`. That method (`toolbar/Base.mjs:490`) returns `[this.createActionSpacerConfig(), ...configs]`, and the spacer (`toolbar/Base.mjs:530`) is `{module: Component, cls: ['neo-toolbar-action-spacer'], flex: 1, isToolbarActionSpacer: true}` — a plain `Neo.component.Base`, hence the `neo-component-*` id.

So the live item list is `[Save, Close, spacer, Undo, Redo]` — **five**, not two.

`WorkspaceController.syncTopologyBar()` (`apps/workstation/view/WorkspaceController.mjs:148`) assumes two:

```javascript
bar.items.slice(me.constructor.authoredTopologyButtonCount).forEach(item => item.destroy());
bar.items.length = me.constructor.authoredTopologyButtonCount;
recovery.length && bar.add(recovery);
```

Two independent faults compound:

1. **`slice(2)` selects toolbar-owned items.** `authoredTopologyButtonCount = 2` counts what the *view* wrote in `items`, but the array it indexes also contains what the *toolbar* materialised from `actions`. The spacer and both action buttons are destroyed.
2. **Neither line maintains the vdom.** `component.Base#destroy(updateParentVdom=false, ...)` defaults its first parameter to `false`, so nothing removes the child's node from the parent. `bar.items.length = 2` is a raw array truncation that bypasses `container.Base#removeAt`, the only path that splices `items` **and** `getVdomItemsRoot().cn` together (`container/Base.mjs:945-947`). `items.length =` appears exactly twice in the repo; the other (`list/Buffered.mjs:840`) trims a recycling pool that owns no vdom.

The docblock above the declaration asserts a guarantee the code does not hold:

> `// Exactly WorkspaceController.authoredTopologyButtonCount items: the controller replaces everything after them and must not be able to destroy these.`

It is true of the two authored buttons and false of everything the toolbar adds after them.

**The engine already owns this operation.** `toolbar.Base` flags every item it owns (`isToolbarAction`, `isToolbarActionSpacer`, `isToolbarActionContribution`) and exposes `getActionItems()`, `getActionSpacer()`, `getAction(name)`, `addActionContribution()` / `removeActionContribution()`, and `syncActions()` — the last documented as replacing the action group *"while preserving every ordinary item"*, implemented over `removeAt`. A consumer that needs to maintain its own subset of a toolbar's items has an identity-based vocabulary available and does not need index arithmetic.

## Why CI is green

`test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/WorkspaceController.spec.mjs:129` builds its own toolbar:

```javascript
const bar = Neo.create(Toolbar, {
    items    : [{ntype: 'button', handler: 'saveTopology',  text: 'Save workspace'},
                {ntype: 'button', handler: 'closeTopology', text: 'Close workspace'}],
    reference: 'topology-toolbar'
});
```

No `actions`. So no spacer, no action items, `bar.items.length === 2`, `slice(2)` is empty, and **the destroy path never executes in any test**. The spec's own comment claims the opposite — *"A real toolbar, so `bar.add` and `item.destroy` are the engine's and not a double's"* — and the toolbar class is real, but the configuration under test is not the one the view ships.

The view's real declaration is asserted in a **different** file (`Workspace.spec.mjs`), so no arm anywhere relates `authoredTopologyButtonCount` to what the toolbar actually materialises. The constant is a claim about another file that nothing checks.

## The Fix

`syncTopologyBar` stops addressing items by position and addresses them by identity.

1. Tag the derived buttons at creation (`isTopologyRecoveryButton: true`).
2. Remove previously-derived buttons with `bar.remove(item, true, true)` — which routes through `removeAt` and keeps `items` and `getVdomItemsRoot().cn` in step — instead of `destroy()` + `items.length =`.
3. Insert new ones ahead of the action spacer via `bar.getActionSpacer()`, so the recovery buttons sit with the other ordinary items rather than past a `flex: 1` spacer on the far side of Undo/Redo.
4. **Delete** `WorkspaceController.authoredTopologyButtonCount`, its docblock, and the view-side comment that references it. The count exists only to serve the positional arithmetic being removed; identity-based removal cannot drift against the view.

Files: `apps/workstation/view/WorkspaceController.mjs`, `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` (comment only), `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/WorkspaceController.spec.mjs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — the fixture is the view's declaration, not an analogue.** The controller spec builds its toolbar from `Workspace.prototype.createTopologyBar()` (or asserts equivalence to it), so `actions` and the spacer are present. This arm must be shown **red before the fix and green after** — a fixture that cannot reproduce the defect certifies nothing.
- [ ] **AC-2 — the toolbar's own items survive a sync.** After `syncTopologyBar()` runs with participants present, `bar.getActionSpacer()` is non-null and `bar.getAction('undo')` / `bar.getAction('redo')` both resolve to live, undestroyed instances.
- [ ] **AC-3 — `items` and `vdom.cn` stay aligned.** After a sync, and again after a resync that removes every participant, `bar.items.length === bar.getVdomItemsRoot().cn.length`, and every `componentId` in `getVdomItemsRoot().cn` resolves through `ComponentManager.get()`. This is the invariant whose violation produced the reported error, so it is asserted directly rather than via the symptom.
- [ ] **AC-4 — the authored head still survives.** The existing guarantee holds: a resync that removes every participant leaves `saveTopology` / `closeTopology` in place. Retained from #18545's arm, which was correct about the head.
- [ ] **AC-5 — `authoredTopologyButtonCount` is gone.** `git grep -n authoredTopologyButtonCount` returns nothing. Positive control: the AC-2/AC-3 arms pass without it, so removal is demonstrated rather than asserted.
- [ ] **AC-6 — the operator's symptom is gone at runtime.** Workstation boots with no `Component not found for id` error in the App Worker console. Verified against a live instance, not only in the unit tier — the unit tier is what missed it.

## Out of Scope

- **`VDom.syncVdomState:451` maps `getVdom` over every child before filtering `removeDom`.** A `removeDom: true` placeholder whose component is gone would throw on the `map` even though the very next line would discard it. That is a real ordering question but it is not this defect (the orphan here is not `removeDom`), and the throw is what made this findable. Not touched.
- **Reverting #18546.** The view-owns-structure direction is right; only the controller's removal mechanics are wrong.
- **The portal live-preview drag-zone symptom** @tobiu reported in the same message. CSS parity was checked and is complete (242 source SCSS files, 0 missing built CSS), so "missing CSS" is unlikely, but no positive finding exists yet. Separate ticket if it survives investigation.
- **`WorkspaceSet` publishing a membership signal.** `syncTopologyBar`'s docblock already records that a participant registered after boot gains no buttons until reload. Unchanged here.

## Avoided Traps

- **Raising `authoredTopologyButtonCount` to 5.** Restores the invariant by coincidence and breaks the moment the view adds an item, the toolbar contributes an action, or `actions` changes length. It also encodes toolbar-internal layout into a consumer constant.
- **Passing `destroy(true)` to update the parent vdom.** Fixes the orphan stubs while still destroying the toolbar's spacer and actions — the symptom goes quiet and Undo/Redo stay gone. Treating the throw as the defect rather than as the detector.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. No ADR governs toolbar item ownership; this restores an existing engine contract rather than changing one.
